transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-13
Start time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20260313-GLC-9182
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Ellen (GlacierOps Head of MLOps), Ravi (Cloud Eng), Sofia (Security), Marco (Dev Lead), Jules (note taker)

Summary: Quick immersion / access and runbook alignment for GlacierOps pilot. Covered host vs dedicated deployment options, network access (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), SSO flow, initial benchmark plan, and success metrics for pilot. Action items assigned and weekly standups agreed.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining really appreciate you making time, we wanted to keep this short and practical, quick intro round robin then we'll walk through access and the pilot runbook
[00:18] Ellen Park: hi all, Ellen here, happy to kick off, main goal is to validate latency and cost for our paraphrase+retrieval pipeline and confirm we can meet the SOC2 controls before we expand
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Ravi, cloud infra, I'll handle VPC and networking pieces
[00:35] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia, security, I'll own compliance ask and audit logs requirements
[00:40] Marco Li: Marco, dev lead, focusing on integration and runbook execution
[00:45] Maya Chen: great, I'm Maya AE, Daniel will cover the technical plan, Priya will manage timelines and runbooks on our side
[00:55] Daniel Ruiz: hey all, quick note, we'll start with Hosted API but prepare a Dedicated plan in parallel; that lets you spin up a small dedicated pool later if the perf delta requires it
[01:10] Marco Li: short question, hosted API is fine for POC but we have data residency constraints for production, does Redwood support VPC/private deployments?
[01:20] Maya Chen: yes, Private (VPC) deployment is supported and we've done on-prem hybrid for a few fintechs. For pilot, we usually do hosted or dedicated in your chosen region then switch to Private for production, we can share a checklist
[01:34] Daniel Ruiz: on the technical side, we want to capture: expected QPS, typical sequence lengths, caching opportunities (we recommend prefix caching for retrieval workflows), and target p95 latency budget so we can tune batching/kv cache
[01:50] Ellen Park: p95 under 250ms is our stretch, 400ms is acceptable; token budget's roughly 200–400 tokens per request, 30 requests per second average during spikes
[02:05] Daniel Ruiz: got it. that'll shape kernel selection and batching; we'll propose a quantization profile and batching window. For the dev benchmark we can run with a 4xT4 pool or equivalent — but if you want realistic numbers we should run on your dev gpus
[02:22] Ravi Patel: we can provide a small GPU node pool in dev — will need the CIDR and a short list of egress/ingress ports/ips
[02:30] Maya Chen: perfect, Daniel will send the network snippet. Priya, want to cover timeline?
[02:38] Priya Nair: sure, recommended cadence: week 0 access + config, week 1 lightweight benchmark, week 2 end-to-end integration with retrieval, week 3 security review and pilot sign-off; weekly 30m standups is what worked for similar customers
[02:55] Ellen Park: that seems fine, we have a cross-functional review the week after next so if we can have security docs before then that would be helpful
[03:05] Sofia Alvarez: specifically I need audit log retention policy, KMS integration options, and SAML metadata for SSO testing. we also need to know whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM
[03:18] Maya Chen: yes to KMS and SIEM forwarding — Redwood Private allows customer-managed KMS; hosted supports envelope encryption and audit export. I'll share the SSO doc and security pack after this call
[03:32] Daniel Ruiz: small callout — for SIEM forwarding we usually push logs to a syslog endpoint or S3 export; we can map fields in the audit log to your SIEM schema
[03:42] Marco Li: regarding authentication for dev benchmarks, what's the recommended auth flow? we prefer short-lived tokens rather than embedding keys in code
[03:50] Daniel Ruiz: short-lived tokens via our SDK and SAML-backed sessions is the usual pattern. For VPC/private setups we also support instance role-based auth inside the private network
[04:02] Jules: (note) someone asked about canary and rollback for model rollouts?
[04:06] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallbacks to a cheaper model variant if a latency/quality regression is detected; we'll demo that in the next session
[04:18] Ellen Park: ok good, we want a guardrail so customer-facing features don't degrade if a new model has a regression
[04:24] Daniel Ruiz: we'll configure automatic fallback policies tied to latency and token cost thresholds; optionally A/B for quality checks
[04:35] Maya Chen: let's pivot to access: two paths — we can give hosted API keys for quick test or set up a temporary VPC peering/PrivateLink for the dev pool. what's your preference Ravi?
[04:48] Ravi Patel: temp peering sounds better so tests reflect real network path; we can open a dev subnet for Redwood to reach and run tests from there
[04:56] Daniel Ruiz: perfect — we'll need the peering proposal and your CIDR; if peering isn't allowed we can do an outbound-only tunnel and still attach to your dev SGs
[05:05] Maya Chen: I'll put the network template in the follow-up email. Also want to confirm stakeholders for sign-off — Ellen and Sofia, correct?
[05:13] Ellen Park: yes myself and Sofia for security, Marco will approve dev integration, Ravi will sign off on network
[05:20] Maya Chen: great. any blockers on credentials or onboarding documents right now?
[05:25] Marco Li: none yet, but can you attach a short sample of the API call shape and error codes so our devs can stub clients quickly?
[05:33] Daniel Ruiz: yes we'll include sample SDK calls and error semantics; note that streaming payloads and function-calling are supported but for initial bench we'll do non-streaming to simplify metrics
[05:44] Sofia Alvarez: a quick question on data retention — for logs and for embeddings, what retention windows do you support? we might need 12 months for auditability
[05:55] Maya Chen: hosted default is 30 days but can be extended with an add-on; Private gives you full control for retention policies. We'll include options with costs in the follow-up
[06:05] Ellen Park: pricing — high level is fine but we'll need a pilot cost estimate with expected token volume and an estimate for dedicated capacity if needed
[06:15] Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll model two scenarios: hosted pilot cost and a reserved Dedicated 1-node baseline. Daniel will provide perf estimates to inform that
[06:24] Daniel Ruiz: in terms of perf tuning we'll look at sequence length distribution — if most requests are <200 tokens we can bias for low-latency kernels; if there are long tails we'll suggest an LRU kv cache policy and different batching windows
[06:37] Marco Li: can you call out the change in cost when we enable kv cache vs not? that's a knob we want to understand
[06:43] Daniel Ruiz: yes kv cache often reduces token compute for repeated prompts, it can lower per-request cost by 10–30% depending on hit rate; we'll estimate for your retrieval pattern after we see traces
[06:55] Jules: (note) someone mentioned compliance artifacts — what exactly will Redwood provide for SOC2 / ISO?
07:00] Sofia Alvarez: (overlap) I need the evidence list not just the policy statements
[07:04] Maya Chen: Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II report summaries under NDA, ISO summary, encryption architecture diagrams, and we maintain audit logs with tamper-evident export. We'll route the compliance pack through your security channel
[07:18] Ravi Patel: on networking, one practical ask — will Redwood require inbound rules for any IP ranges or is the peering fully internal?
[07:26] Daniel Ruiz: with VPC peering it's internal, no public inbound. With PrivateLink you only need to allow the endpoint. We'll be explicit in the network checklist
[07:35] Ellen Park: ok good. Let's talk about acceptance criteria — what's the short list for pilot success?
[07:43] Maya Chen: suggested pilot acceptance: 1) p95 latency under 400ms for retrieval+generation flow, 2) no functional regression in top-5 retrieval coherence (we'll use your prompt set), 3) audit log and SSO integration verified, 4) cost within modeled threshold (±20%)
[08:05] Marco Li: that's sensible. we'll add monitoring hooks and a runbook to escalate incidents during the pilot
[08:12] Priya Nair: Priya to own runbook template and weekly cadence, I'll share a short-runbook example after the call
[08:19] Ellen Park: can we add one more stake — a smoke test for throughput at 2x expected QPS for 15 minutes?
[08:27] Daniel Ruiz: yes we can run that as a stress profile in week 1 benchmark. we'll make sure there's an automatic fallback if latency spikes
[08:35] Maya Chen: final part — scheduling next sessions: SE deep-dive for VPC+bench on Tue 2026-03-16 at 11am PT?
[08:44] Ravi Patel: works for me
[08:46] Ellen Park: works
[08:47] Maya Chen: great, I'll schedule and include the network template and security pack. any other risks we didn't cover?
[08:54] Sofia Alvarez: one risk — third-party model auditing if we end up using an external model, need contract language for model provenance
[09:02] Maya Chen: noted, we'll surface model provenance info and licensing notes. in many cases we onboard open models and provide checksums and provenance metadata
[09:12] Marco Li: thanks everyone, that's helpful. can we get the initial credentials and a test key so devs can stub?
[09:20] Maya Chen: yes hosted test keys available within 24 hours; for peering it will take a bit longer. I'll cc the keys to Marco and Jules once issued
[09:28] Priya Nair: recap and next steps: Maya to send security pack and network checklist (due 3/16), Daniel to run dev benchmark and send perf numbers (due 3/20), Ravi to share CIDR and dev node access (due 3/15), Sofia to enumerate required compliance artifacts (due 3/17), weekly standups starting 3/23.
[09:52] Ellen Park: thanks all, excited to get this running
[09:55] Maya Chen: thanks everyone we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs

Meeting end.
